title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'Teichmüller tower' notes, specifically the construction of the maps between moduli of curves attached to a specialization of dual graphs ('graphes MD', presumably Mumford–Deligne stable graphs) G -> G' = G/C. Here C is a set of free edges (nodes) of G.

Previous page: X is a nodal curve of type G. X~ is its partial normalization at C, and C~ is the set of preimages of C. Around each point of C~ one chooses small disjoint closed holomorphic disks D_x~ with real-analytic boundary. Grothendieck conjectures that the space of such choices is contractible, so the forgetful map M_G^C -> M_G is a homotopy equivalence. Removing the open disks gives X_1, a holomorphic surface with boundary, with one boundary circle for each point of C~.

This page:
(1) Each boundary circle d_x~ X = dD_x~ is a torsor under the circle group U = {|z|=1}. This comes from uniformizing the disk by the unit disk with centre sent to x~, which is unique up to rotation. The orientation coming from U is opposite to the boundary orientation induced by X_1, as it should be, since it is the boundary orientation of the disk.
(2) Conversely, (X, C~ marked) is recovered from X_1 together with these U-torsor structures. The cone on a U-torsor circle is canonically a holomorphic disk with centre, and gluing it back ('chirurgie holomorphe') restores X with the marked centres.
(3) For a node x in C with preimages x', x'', consider Isom^-_U(T_x', T_x''). These are the anti-isomorphisms, i.e. bijections compatible with z -> z^{-1}, equivalently orientation-reversing identifications of the two boundary circles. This set is a U-torsor, isomorphic to Isom_U(T_x'^{-1}, T_x'') = T_x' ∧ T_x'' (contracted product), symmetric in x' and x''. Call it T_x.
(4) NB: T_x~ is canonically the circle of real tangent directions (T_{X~,x~} minus 0)/R*+. This is independent of the choice of disk, so T_x is the unit circle of T_x' ⊗_C T_x''. That tensor product is the normal line to the boundary stratum at X, the classical smoothing parameter.
(5) P_C = Π_{x in C} T_x is a U^C-torsor.

Next page: as X varies, the P_C form a U^C-torsor M~_G^C over M_G^C. Gluing the boundary circles of X_1 according to t = (t_x) defines a smooth-at-C curve X'_t of type G'. This gives a morphism of topoi M~_G^C -> M_G'. Then 1 -> Z^C -> π1(M~) -> π1(M_G) -> 1, and π1(M~) maps to π1(M_G'). The Z^C are the Dehn twists about the vanishing cycles.

In modern terms: the U^C-torsor is the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of the stratum Δ_G in M̄. Equivalently, it is the torus bundle of the real oriented blow-up of M̄ along the boundary divisors. The gluing map is twist-plumbing. The resulting π1 homomorphisms are the structure maps of the Teichmüller groupoid tower: boundary inclusions of mapping class groups, extended by twists.
errors: No substantive errors. One caution: gluing two real-analytic boundary circles by an orientation-reversing real-analytic map gives a well-defined Riemann surface. However, the 'size' parameter of the smoothing is hidden in the choice of disks rather than in |t|, so the map M~ -> M_G' is not literally the standard plumbing zw=t. It is only homotopically equivalent to it (and to the real-blow-up boundary).

The NB writes T*_{X~,x~}/R*+. If this denoted the cotangent space, the torsor would be the inverse of the boundary torsor. Most likely the star means the tangent space minus 0, in which case it is consistent.

ideas.what: Boundary circles of removed holomorphic disks carry canonical U-torsor structures, identified with the unit tangent circle at the puncture; the surface with C~ marked is recovered by holomorphic coning/surgery

missed.claim: The torsor T_x' ∧ T_x'' of anti-isomorphisms of tangent circles at a node, taken over all edges, is exactly the topological counterpart of the tangential base points at the boundary of M̄_{g,n}. These were used later by Deligne and Ihara–Nakamura for the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower. Grothendieck builds the topological version (the oriented real blow-up torsor) directly into his construction of tower maps, years before Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov.
missed.quote: Isom^-_U(T_x', T_x'') ≃ Isom_U(T_x'^{-1}, T_x'') ... on aura un U-torseur T_x = ∧ T_x~ ... T_x~ s'identifie aussi au cercle des tangentes ... (ce qui est indép. du choix des D_x~)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, unpublished, explicit form of the 'framed' (circle-decorated) boundary of moduli used in modular operads and in the topological Teichmüller groupoid. This is mostly of historical interest; the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early (c. 1978–81) explicit construction of the circle-torsor or real-blow-up boundary of strata, with twist-gluing, used to define the Teichmüller tower maps. This anticipates Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov and parallels tangential base points. The content is now standard, but this precise formulation is not in Grothendieck's published texts.
transcription_corrections: The insertion near the 'X' line likely reads 'avec la partie C~ marquée' (tilde C), marking the centres.
In the NB, 'T^*_{X~,x~}' probably denotes the tangent space minus the origin (T minus 0), not the cotangent space; 'cercle des tangentes' may be 'cercle des demi-tangentes'.
'par la symétrie [?]' is perhaps 'symétriquement' (the identification with T_x' ∧ T_x'').
In T_x = ∧_{x~ ∈ C_x} T_x~, the index set C_x is the fibre of C~ over x (the two points x', x'').
